summary:
Round 2 does what it claims on the corpora:
- Whole-design Y, Z, random, edge and snapped moves move no G anywhere.
- The twin, speck, id and grip-nudge cases are closed.
- The as-built drift is exactly what fixer U reported, and the goldens, §5.5, the mirror figures and the digest all reproduce.

Two majors stand.

**(A) A hidden part can still change a tier, and existing tests now fail on official seeds.** The new tie centre counts cleaned parts. A player can build this with the editor alone:
- Ctrl+D a part and type the copy 0.002 across. The verdict cleans one of the two.
- Ctrl+D the cleaned copy in place. That duplicate is hidden too.

The verdict then keeps the other copy, or both copies:
- Plausible #1940: Sharpening 0.1950 Normal → 0.2099 Hard.
- C09: G moves 0.0143 and the balance shown to the player moves.

f7ac37d and round 1 move none of this. The project's own property Cover (d), "an exact copy first or last … every other reading the same bits", now fails on PROP_BASE_SEED 0x0C0FFEE1 and 0x2468ACE0. That makes §14.6's "every case holds on six PROP_BASE_SEEDs" false, along with §4.4/§4.5's "no hidden part moves the balance" and the "G the same" wording.

A tried one-line repair counts a tied part standing exactly on an earlier one only once:
- It reads every fixture, generated and plausible design bit for bit as now.
- It passes --quick unchanged and restores Cover (d) on the three failing seeds.
- It closes the in-place duplicate, at no measurable cost.

A duplicate nudged 0.0005 off the copy still flips #1940, so the SPEC must state that reach either way.

**(B) A false sentence in §17.2.** It says near twins stacked in z no longer swap under the Z mirror. Under round 2 they are twins about their own centre and do swap. #1940 with a near copy plays Hard in its Z image; f7ac37d and round 1 keep it Normal.

Minors:
- Six surviving mutants of my 22. One is now killed by a tried pin; the five constant-value survivors have no pin tried.
- §5.5 leaves out C11 and X02.
- §4.4's half-RANK_Q and "only typed digits" wording.
- The factor bounds hold for exact moves, not the editor's snapped moves.
- One blade-copy assertion loosened to a 5 % band.
- Timing:
  - T-PERF-01 fails only under load. Run quiet it passes, but worst valid 8 reads 57.32–57.33 ms, above the lead's 57 ms gate, as on every tree.
  - --quick takes 30.04–30.35 s at 4–19 % load, just over §14.1's 30 s.

A hidden part steers a tier, the shown balance and an existing property. This is an editor-only regression against f7ac37d and shift-r1, and it makes SPEC statements false.

The verdict's tie centre is the mean over every tied part, cleaned ones included. The construction uses only the editor:
1. Ctrl+D a part in place, then move the copy 0.002 along X or Z. The verdict cleans one of the pair as Enclosed.
2. Ctrl+D the cleaned copy in place. This exact copy is itself cleaned.
3. The duplicate pulls the pair's centre to its side, so live keeps the other copy, or keeps both.

issues.fix:
Code (tried in var/dp; diff in scratchpad shift-v2-2/out/repair_dp_src.diff). In acrossTies, before the sums, mark a part that stands exactly where an earlier tied part stands, and skip it in the mean:

```lua
local again: { boolean } = table.create(N, false)
for i = 2, N do
	local p = parts[i]
	local kp = keys[p.index]
	for j = 1, i - 1 do
		local q = parts[j]
		local kq = keys[q.index]
		if q.cx == p.cx and q.cz == p.cz and kq[1] == kp[1] and kq[2] == kp[2]
			and (not bySlot or q.slot == p.slot) and (kept == nil or kept[q.index] == kept[p.index])
		then
			again[i] = true
			break
		end
	end
end
```

Then sum only `if not again[j] and …`. Its comment says each place is counted once.

Results of the trial:
- --quick: 727 pass, 0 fail, with no test changed.
- The 136 fixtures, 200 generated and all 33,389 plausible designs read bit for bit as live.
- Cover (d) passes on 0x0C0FFEE1, 0x2468ACE0 and 0x600DCAFE.
- In-place duplicates swap nothing: fixtures 21 pairs, generated 59, plausible sample 804. #1940 stays 0.1950.
- Cost: dp/live per-case median 0.9959, sum 0.9949, at 4–31 % load.

It does not close a duplicate nudged 0.0005 past the copy. #1940 still goes 0.1950 → 0.2099 Hard, and F3 and C09 still move. So also state the reach, in §4.4, §0.5, §5's third limit, §5.6, O11 (j), §17.2, M3-notes and M3-spec-changes, in place of 'G the same (where measured)':

'built on near copies a player can see (a part copied 0.002 across, a copy of the copy hidden 0.0005 beyond it), it decides which copy is kept, or keeps both, and so moves G, a tier and the balance: plausible #1940 Sharpening 0.1950 Normal → 0.2099 Hard; C09 both copies kept, Sharpening 0.1904 → 0.1761; f7ac37d none'.

In §4.4 l.1096 and §4.5 l.1117, add 'but through which of two near copies a hidden tied part leaves kept (§4.4)'.

Also tried, and not recommended: the midrange (min+max)/2 variant (out/variant_midrange_src.diff). It has the same closures and plausible drift on 3 fullers, but it makes every tie group's two extremes twins about the centre, and Verdict.spec's ranked case fails on it.

A SPEC statement is made false by round 2's ranks. l.4853 reads: '|z| comes before z in the rank as |x| before x, so near twins stacked in z no longer swap under the Z mirror: 545 of 8,000 tangles did'.

Under round 2 a pair of near twins (tied on volume, slot and height) is twins about its own centre, so the mirror image swaps which one the verdict keeps.

Measured (work/mirnear.luau), each design with a near copy and no hidden part, in its mirror image:
- #1940 plus its middle plate copied 0.002 along Z: the Z image keeps the other plate. Sharpening 0.1950 Normal → 0.2099 Hard, Hammering 0.1673 → 0.1786.
- C09 plus its blade core copied 0.002 along X: the X image keeps both copies. Hammering 0.3201 → 0.3114, Sharpening 0.1904 → 0.1732.
- F3: 0.4423 → 0.4427. Gen 200: 0.2110 → 0.2156.

f7ac37d and shift-r1: every image reads its original exactly.

The swap is O11 (l)'s class, but this sentence says it no longer happens, and O11 (l)'s figures (22 X, 25 Z tiers) come from a corpus that has no near copies.

issues.file: SPEC.md §4.4 l.941-942 and l.954-958 (and O11 (j), §17.2 'within half a RANK_Q')
issues.problem:
Two wordings are inexact.

1. 'Parts whose heights or places lie within half a RANK_Q of each other, which only typed sub-1e-9 digits give, tie and fall to the index'. Values within half a step tie only when they round to one step: heights 1.0000000004 and 1.0000000006 do not tie. And ordinary arithmetic (1.4 + 0.2 beside 1.6) gives such ties too.
2. 'keeps every height and place but one lying on a half step, which only typed digits reach'. The next sentence quotes free drags reaching it (4 of 12.8 million), and §11.8 leaves free drag values untouched.

The class is named, so this is wording only.
issues.fix:
'Parts whose heights or places round to one step of RANK_Q (within a RANK_Q of each other, which typed sub-1e-9 digits or an ulp of arithmetic give) tie …'.

'… but one lying on a half step, which typed digits reach, and a free drag about 3e-7 of the time a pair …'.
